verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev documents a management API with two authentication modes: an environment secretKey or a personal access token. It also documents a TriggerClient for targeting projects and environments, triggering tasks from a backend, and using run handles to check status, cancel and retry, so a programmatic or AI-native user can drive the product through it. missing for 10: no machine-readable OpenAPI spec was found (the probes returned 404 at the standard paths), and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration that the API works in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: There are two methods of authenticating with the management API: using a named API key associated with a specific environment in a project (`secretKey`), or using a personal access token
If a single process needs to talk to more than one Trigger.dev project, environment, or preview branch, use `new TriggerClient({...})` for each target instead of `configure()`.
You can use the handle to check the status of the task, cancel and retry it.
